applies_why: The judge text addresses the D4 vs C2 Luke 2:48-49 collision by treating Mary's phrase as qualified by the child's reply, so it engages the pressed-witness weighing the rule governs.
quote: Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': (1) the judge's own reason must compare the whole pressed chain with the answering chain by footing; (2) merely citing prior sections where such a comparison appears could satisfy the rule. The judge added its own verse-level qualification, so it took the first reading.
why: The judge text gives a verse-level qualification of Luke 2:48 by Luke 2:49 as the reason, rather than weighing the pressed chain against the answering chain by footing.
